```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(knitr)

# ---- load everything this notebook uses (all made by the scripts, nothing is calculated from raw files here) ----
SampleMeta <- read_csv(here("data", "mpw_sample_meta.csv"))                          # one row per sample: field + lab data
RespoMeta  <- read_csv(here("data", "respirometry", "mpw", "mpw_respo_meta.csv"))    # respo times, notes, exclude
RespoR_PR  <- read_csv(here("data", "respirometry", "mpw", "processed", "mpw_PnR_rates.csv")) # rates from respo_rates_plots.R

# samples left out of results = anything with text in the "exclude" column
excluded <- RespoMeta %>% filter(!is.na(exclude)) %>% distinct(sample_ID, exclude)

# which instrument each chamber channel belongs to
device_of <- function(ch) case_when(ch %in% 1:4   ~ "Oxy-4 #087 (ch 1-4)",
                                    ch %in% 5:8   ~ "Oxy-4 #082 (ch 5-8)",
                                    ch %in% 9:12  ~ "Oxy-4 #100 (ch 9-12)",
                                    ch %in% 13:22 ~ "Oxy-10 (ch 13-22)")
```

## 1. Overview

**Question:** How does water column metabolism (respiration and photosynthesis of the plankton community) change across a groundwater gradient at the Kapo'o tidepool at Shark's Cove?

**Site:** Kapo'o tidepool, North Shore of Oʻahu. The tidepool is shallow and lagoon-like (max ~4 ft deep). It receives submarine groundwater discharge (SGD) linked to the beach restroom, which is likely carrying sewage. Samples were also taken outside the pool in the adjacent cove and ocean.

**Design:** 6 sampling days (Oct 1–6, 2026). Each day at dawn, one sampler collected 10 samples inside the pool and one collected 10 outside (5 cove, 5 ocean), plus one blank. Each sample was split into subsamples for respirometry, chl-a, nutrients, fDOM, flow cytometry (FCM) and total alkalinity (TA).

**Respirometry:** PreSens Oxy-4 (×3) and Oxy-10, 473 mL chambers

Collaborator: Mālama Pūpūkea-Waimea (MPW)
Field Team: ...

## 4. Respirometry processing

Rates are calculated in two steps:

1. `scripts/respirometry/respo_LoLinR.R`: run **once per sample day**. Cuts each raw O₂ file to its dark and light windows (from `mpw_respo_meta.csv`), drops the acclimation period, thins the data, and fits LoLinR local regressions (Olito et al. 2017). Saves `processed/mpw_RespoR_D#.csv` and diagnostic PDFs in `output/mpw/respirometry/D#/`. Slow if long day and thinned to every 10th row.
2. `scripts/respirometry/respo_rates_plots.R`: converts slopes to µmol O₂ hr⁻¹ using chamber volume, calculates respiration, net and gross photosynthesis, and makes plots.

```{r}
#| label: settings-table
tribble(
  ~day, ~thin_n, ~acclim_sec, ~note,
  "D1", 10, 1800, "",
  "D2", 10, 1800, "",
  "D3", 20, 1800, "rerun 10/21 (session closed before saving), thinned to every 20th",
  "D4", 10, 1800, "",
  "D5", 20, 1800,    "merged export from problematic run;long run so thinned every 20th",
  "D6", 20, 1800, "rerun 10/21 (session closed before saving), thinned to every 20th",
) %>% kable(caption = "Processing settings per day. thin_n = keep every Nth row; acclim_sec = seconds dropped at the start of each phase")
```

::: {.callout-note}
Days were processed with different thinning (every 10th vs 20th row). A test on D5 showed slopes barely change between the two, but before publishing, all days should be rerun with the same settings.
:::

```{r}
#| label: loop-key-lines
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: show
# the key lines inside the loop in respo_LoLinR.R (shown, not run)
data <- Respo.Data1 %>%
  filter(Time >= start_time & Time <= stop_time) %>%   # dark or light window from metadata
  arrange(Time) %>%
  mutate(t_sec = as.numeric(difftime(Time, first(Time), units = "secs"))) %>%
  filter(t_sec > acclim_sec) %>%                        # drop acclimation period
  filter(row_number() %% thin_n == 0)                   # thin the data

rankLocReg(xall = data$t_sec, yall = data$Value, alpha = 0.2, method = "pc")  # LoLinR fit
```

## 5. Quality control

**Rule for now:** a sample is excluded if O₂ *rises* in the dark (respiration < 0), which is not biologically possible. Additionally if the probe clearly failed (bad calibration D1). Excluded samples are marked in the `exclude` column of `mpw_respo_meta.csv` and will be revisited.

```{r}
#| label: exclusion-counts
excluded %>% count(exclude, name = "samples") %>%
  kable(caption = "Samples excluded so far, by reason")
```

### Failures by instrument

```{r}
#| label: failures-by-device
resp <- RespoR_PR %>%
  filter(PR == "Respiration", !str_detect(sample_ID, "BLK")) %>%
  mutate(R_up = Values < 0,
         device = device_of(chamber_channel))

resp %>%
  group_by(device) %>%
  summarise(samples = n(), n_R_up = sum(R_up), percent = round(100 * mean(R_up))) %>%
  kable(caption = "Samples where O2 rose in the dark, by instrument (blanks not included)")
```

```{r}
#| label: failures-by-chamber
#| fig-height: 3.5
resp %>%
  group_by(chamber_channel, device) %>%
  summarise(percent_R_up = 100 * mean(R_up), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(chamber_channel), y = percent_R_up, fill = device)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "Chamber channel", y = "% of runs with O2 rising in the dark", fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

**What this shows:** 34 of the 48 sample failures were on the Oxy-10 (channels 13–22), plus all 4 working blanks, which were also on the Oxy-10 (52 "R up" in total). It reads high in both phases: the median dark slope on the Oxy-10 is about +0.13 µmol L⁻¹ h⁻¹ versus about −0.2 on the Oxy-4s. Every blank was on the Oxy-10, and all of them rose in the dark (BLK1's probe failed outright). The Oxy-4 failures were mostly runs where the chamber cooled slightly during the dark phase.

```{r}
#| label: blanks
RespoR_PR %>%
  filter(str_detect(sample_ID, "BLK")) %>%
  select(run_block, sample_ID, chamber_channel, PR, Values) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = PR, values_from = Values) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>%
  kable(caption = "Blanks (umol O2/hr). All on the Oxy-10; BLK1 = probe failure")
```

## 6. Results so far

::: {.callout-warning}
Preliminary. Excluded samples are removed, rates are **not** blank-corrected, and most remaining data come from the Oxy-4s (see QC).
:::

```{r}
#| label: plot-data
sgd_cutoff_m <- 10   # lagoon samples closer than this to the SGD = "near_SGD", the rest = "T"

plot_data <- RespoR_PR %>%
  left_join(SampleMeta %>% select(sample_ID, habitat, dist_to_sgd_m, time_collected), by = "sample_ID") %>%
  filter(habitat != "blank") %>%
  filter(!sample_ID %in% excluded$sample_ID) %>%
  mutate(habitat_sgd = case_when(habitat == "lagoon" & dist_to_sgd_m <  sgd_cutoff_m ~ "near_SGD",
                                 habitat == "lagoon" & dist_to_sgd_m >= sgd_cutoff_m ~ "T",
                                 habitat == "cove"  ~ "C",
                                 habitat == "ocean" ~ "O"),
         habitat_sgd = factor(habitat_sgd, levels = c("near_SGD", "T", "C", "O")),
         PR = factor(PR, levels = c("Respiration", "NetPhoto", "GrossPhoto"),
                     labels = c("Respiration", "Net photosynthesis", "Gross photosynthesis")))
```

### By habitat and distance to SGD

```{r}
#| label: pr-by-habitat
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 9
plot_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = habitat_sgd, y = Values)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.5) +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = run_block), width = 0.12, alpha = 0.8, size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~PR, nrow = 1) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  labs(x = paste0("near_SGD = tidepool < ", sgd_cutoff_m, " m from SGD, T = rest of tidepool, C = cove, O = ocean"),
       y = expression(paste(mu, "mol O"[2], " hr"^-1)), color = "Day") +
  theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

## 7. Questions for advisor / lab

1. **Oxy-10 drift:** 71% of Oxy-10 sample runs (34 of 48) show O₂ rising in the dark, and so do all the blanks. Is this a known issue with this unit (calibration, sensor spots, temperature compensation)? Can the blanks be used to correct it instead of excluding 34 samples?
2. **Negative net photosynthesis:** could be real net heterotrophy near the sewage input rather than an error. Exclude only when gross P < 0 or the trace shows an artifact?
3. **Variables to test:** Day, tide and time of day move together. Which driver can this design actually test?
4. **Blank correction and units:** subtract the blank per day? Report per litre and, once chl-a is done, per chl-a?
5. **Consistent processing:** rerun all days at every 20th row?
